newsitem.title: SUDAN: SUDAN SACKS HEAD OF INDUSTRIAL BANK.
newsitem.headline: SUDAN SACKS HEAD OF INDUSTRIAL BANK.

text.p: The Sudanese government has fired the chairman of the board and general manager of el-Nilein Industrial Development Bank, a government newspaper said on Tuesday.

Al-Sudan al-Hadith did not give a reason for the dismissal of Sa'eed Osman Mahjoub, a wealthy engineer who worked in the Gulf for many years before returning to Sudan after Lieutenant General Omar Hassan al-Bashir seized power in a coup in 1989.

A government decree was issued recently appointing Minister of State for Finance and National Economy Sabir Mohammed al-Hassan as the chairman of el-Nilein Industrial Development Bank's board of directors, the newspaper said.
Al-Hassan was once an International Monetary Fund official in Washington.
The decree named Badr al-Din Mahmoud Abbas as the bank's general manager.
El-Nilein Industrial Development Bank group has paid up capital of 566 million Sudanese pound ($388,000) and is the largest industrial bank in Sudan.
The bank's volume of investments in 1995 were 15 billion pounds.
The group was put together as a result of a merger of el-Nilein Bank, Credit Lyonnais and the Industrial Bank of Sudan. The group has over 30 branches in Sudan and abroad.
